title: Sample 2-17: Dots Separating Linear Contents Entries

illustrates.quote: Short-listed or linear contents entries without page numbers are listed at the correct subentry level. (See Sample 2-17: Dots Separating Linear Contents Entries on page 2-43 and Sample 2-18: Listed Unnumbered Contents Entries on page 2-44.)

print.notes: Print original is a photographic reproduction of a real book's cover/title/copyright/contents page (references/_gemini/gold-2-A/page-087.png), not encoded as running text anywhere in the source .txt. Neither independent transcription run modelled it into print.blocks (both left print.blocks empty); this reconciliation viewed the page image directly to confirm the braille.lines transcription and the sample's own title/rule citation, but likewise leaves print.blocks empty -- building a faithful print.blocks model of a photographed book cover is out of this reconciliation's scope (reconciling two existing transcription runs), not a disagreement between them to resolve.

resolution: braille.lines: A and B agree on content; A's version (kept here) retains the source's own leading/internal/trailing blank braille lines verbatim (confirmed by direct re-derivation from source-lines-1390-2934.txt), matching this gold corpus's established convention (see e.g. tests/gold/bana-formats-2016/section-5's own U+2800-filler-line handling); B's version silently strips those blank lines. illustrates.quote: A's rule text was verbatim-correct but scoped to the whole lettered rule (plus, in some files, a stray page-footer line glued in by the extraction) rather than the specific numbered sub-item/cross-reference this example cites; B's own quote field was not a quote at all (it echoed the file's own title/caption). Re-derived directly from source-lines-1390-2934.txt, scoped to exactly the cited rule id.
